facts.statement: The genus Telecrex was described by Wetmore in 1934.
The genus contains two species: Telecrex grangeri and Telecrex peregrinus.
facts.quote: containing two species, Telecrex grangeri (the type species) and Telecrex peregrinus

facts.statement: Telecrex peregrinus was found in France.
facts.quote: while T. peregrinus was found in France

facts.statement: Wetmore originally assigned the genus Telecrex to the family Rallidae in 1934.
facts.quote: The new genus Telecrex was described by Wetmore in 1934 and assigned to the Rallidae

facts.statement: Storrs Olson reexamined the holotype in 1974 and concluded it was an early relative of guineafowl.
facts.quote: In 1974, the holotype was reexamined by Storrs Olson, who concluded that it was in fact an early relative of guineafowl

facts.statement: The holotype of Telecrex peregrinus was collected near Lalbenque in France in the nineteenth century and described by Mlíkovský in 1986.
facts.quote: The holotype of Telecrex peregrinus, NHMW 1988/28/1 was collected near Lalbenque in Lot, France at some point in the nineteenth century and described as a new species by Mlíkovský in 1986

facts.statement: Telecrex peregrinus was larger than Telecrex grangeri.
facts.quote: Telecrex peregrinus was larger in size than Telecrex grangeri

facts.statement: The parent group of Telecrex is Numididae.
Telecrex belongs to the family Numididae.
Telecrex is classified in the class Reptilia.
Telecrex lived between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Bartonian (56 to 37.71 million years ago)
